title_options: How Geckos Walk Up Glass (No Suction, No Glue) 🦎

share.myth: Geckos stick with suction cups or sticky glue on their feet.
share.truth: Their toes carry millions of hairs splitting into about a billion tiny tips; each gets close enough for van der Waals attraction, which works on water-loving and water-repelling surfaces alike (Autumn et al. 2002, PNAS; Huber et al. 2005, PNAS).
share.line: Geckos don't use suction or glue. A billion tiny tips get so close that molecules pull them onto the glass.

facts: Autumn K et al. 2002, PNAS 99:12252: first direct evidence of dry adhesion of gecko setae by van der Waals forces; capillary (wet) adhesion rejected; a single seta adhered equally to hydrophobic and hydrophilic surfaces; the effect depends on tip size and shape.
Huber G et al. 2005, PNAS 102:16293: about one billion spatulae on a Tokay gecko (Ruibal & Ernst 1965); humidity adds to adhesion at the nanoscale, so van der Waals is the main, not the only, force.
Each seta branches into hundreds of spatula tips; geckos detach by peeling their toes up from the tip (digital hyperextension; Autumn et al. 2000, Nature: setae release at about 30 degrees).
description: A gecko runs up glass with no suction cups and no glue. A billion tiny tips on its toes get so close that molecules pull them to the surface. #shorts #science #gecko #physics
sources: Autumn et al. 2002, PNAS 99:12252 (van der Waals adhesion in gecko setae); Huber et al. 2005, PNAS 102:16293 (single spatula measurements); Autumn et al. 2000, Nature 405:681.

scenes.narration: A gecko can run straight up glass. No suction cups. No glue.
Zoom into its toes, and they're covered in millions of tiny hairs.
Each hair splits into hundreds of even tinier tips. About a billion on one gecko.
Each tip gets so close to the glass that a weak pull between molecules, called van der Waals force, takes hold.
One tip's pull is almost nothing. A billion of them together hold the whole gecko.
Tests in two thousand and two showed a single hair sticks just as well to surfaces that love water and ones that repel it. So it's not wet glue.
To let go, the gecko peels its toes up from the tip, like tape.
Geckos don't use suction or glue. A billion tiny tips get so close that molecules pull them onto the glass.
So what would you build if you had gecko feet?
